item.title: A fungus turns beetles into zombies and makes them die on flowers to infect the next generation
item.description: A fungus infects goldenrod soldier beetles, causing them to grip flowers before dying. After death, the fungus alters their bodies, raising wings between midnight and 7 am. These changes occur approximately fifteen to twenty-two hours after the beetles have expired. Infected beetles were found on frost aster and common boneset plants in Arkansas. Fungal outbreaks primarily occurred during autumn when adult beetles are present.

item.title: ‘Ghost’ green mamba rediscovered decades after its 1885 discovery in São Tomé
item.description: Researchers have made an exciting discovery of a long-lost 1885 green mamba specimen from São Tomé Island, previously thought to be missing. Found within a Polish museum's collection, this specimen enables scientists to revisit its taxonomic classification. With physical traits closely matching the western green mamba, this rediscovery ignites curiosity about the survival status of this snake on its native island.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: AI may soon be able to pay for things through UPI without asking every single time
item.description: The potential introduction of AI agents in India for autonomous UPI payments marks a significant advancement in transaction technology. Users would enjoy the convenience of hands-free purchases while having the ability to establish preset instructions and budget limitations. Proposed safety measures, including identity checks and spending restrictions are currently under consideration, reflecting a wider global trend towards automated payment systems.

item.title: Widower Loses Retirement Savings: Online romance scam wipes out $800,000; recovery ploy deepens pain
item.description: After losing $800,000 in an online romance scam following his wife's passing, Simon struggled with debts and taxes related to the stolen money. Authorities linked the funds to a scam operation in Myanmar. Alarmingly, Americans lost $15.9 billion to fraud in 2025, marking a steep rise, with victims often falling prey to further scams by recovery scammers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A West Virginia high school built in 1923 has reopened 103 years later as a 40-room hotel
item.description: A historic high school in West Virginia, originally established in 1923, has been beautifully transformed into a 40-room boutique hotel. The once-abandoned classrooms now serve as cozy guest rooms and inviting lounges, offering visitors a unique stay. This renovation breathes new life into a campus that had been closed for more than ten years, blending its historic charm with contemporary residential design.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK mortgage approvals fall to lowest level since January 2024 as housing demand weakens
item.description: In July, UK mortgage approvals for home purchases hit a new low, highlighting a weakened demand in the housing market amid rising borrowing costs. Additionally, net mortgage borrowing plummeted, falling below the six-month average. While house prices saw slight annual growth, they decreased when adjusted for inflation. Conversely, unsecured consumer borrowing rose, revealing an increasing dependence on credit for everyday spending.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Ranch Shift Protects River: $8m deal secures 1,688-acre Park Ranch; wildlife corridor stays open
item.description: A significant eight million dollar grant has facilitated the acquisition of one thousand six hundred eighty-eight acres of land for public use. This area safeguards a crucial wildlife corridor and an undammed river, enhancing conservation efforts for native fish habitats and seasonal wildlife migration. The Park Ranch, located near Markleeville, transitioned to Alpine County's management in August, with public access planned following the development of a thorough management strategy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rampage Jackson fires cameraman after heated livestream argument takes shocking turn
item.description: Former UFC star Rampage Jackson found himself in a fiery confrontation with his cameraman. The disagreement intensified as they exchanged words about mutual friends and associates, leading Jackson to chase after his cameraman, proclaiming he was terminated. Fortunately, the cameraman evaded any physical altercation. This dramatic encounter was live-streamed, giving viewers an inside look at the unexpected fallout.

item.title: TheBurntPeanut 9/11 joke controversy explained as streamer faces backlash over shocking comment
item.description: TheBurntPeanut is facing backlash after making a 9/11 joke during an Escape from Tarkov stream. The streamer used a model aircraft, a magazine and a bottle to recreate an airplane approaching two towers before joking, “Boom! They hit the second tower!” X users had mixed reactions, with some calling it offensive and others simply calling it “cringy.” His older HasanAbi controversy has also returned to the discussion.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: German Twitch streamer ZoeMatthea’s Gamescom trip takes disturbing turn after alleged stalker reappears
item.description: During her live Gamescom stream, German Twitch streamer ZoeMatthea faced an alleged stalker who has reportedly harassed her for nearly two years. The unsettling encounter unfolded live, capturing the attention of her viewers. Although the police indicated there was not enough evidence to confirm the stalking claims, this incident has brought renewed focus on ZoeMatthea's persistent harassment issues, highlighting the ongoing challenges faced by streamers in maintaining their safety online.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Markiplier to make millions from GoPro investment after company announces $285m Starman merger
item.description: Markiplier could be in for a major payday after GoPro announced its merger with Starman Optical. The YouTuber owns more than 8.5% of GoPro and is the company’s largest individual shareholder outside investment firms and GoPro itself. His stake is estimated at around $9 million, while shareholders are set to receive around $1.14 per share under the deal. The exact payout for Fischbach has not been disclosed yet.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Who is michaelshowscoolthings? Terraria kid gets MrBeast’s support after sharing family update
item.description: Young Instagram creator michaelshowscoolthings is going viral after taking a short break from his Terraria videos after revealing his family has to move to another state due to financial struggles. The creator said he was “just really sad” about the situation. Since then, he has received support from MrBeast, Agent of Chaos, Piques and activist Patricia Arquette. The young gamer is expected to pause his uploads for several days while his family handles the move.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Hasanabi Defends Broke Claim: Streamer disputes X note; says socialism not a poverty cult
item.description: HasanAbi responded after an X Community Note challenged his claim that he was once broke. He said critics ignored the period between college and his first job, while acknowledging that he grew up affluent. HasanAbi also defended his socialist views, arguing that socialism is not about poverty and that wealthy people can support the ideology without contradiction.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Nick White sparks controversy over Morgpie as he says she "easily could be a Trans" on stream
item.description: Morgpie is facing fresh controversy after Kick streamer Nick White commented on her appearance during a livestream. He said some of her looks appeared “too masculine” and that she “easily could be a Trans.” Separate claims from streamer Nick Lee have also resurfaced, but those remain unverified opinions. Here’s what was said, who Morgpie is, and what the available information actually establishes about the controversy.

item.title: Not-Guilty Plea Sparks Clash: Tyler Robinson denies killing Charlie Kirk; Candace Owens attacks influencers
item.description: Candace Owens reacted strongly after Tyler Robinson pleaded not guilty to charges in the Charlie Kirk murder case. Owens criticized commentators who, she said, had portrayed Robinson’s alleged involvement as already established and insisted that the court process must determine the facts. She also predicted that claims made during the controversy would face scrutiny as proceedings continue. Robinson is scheduled to return to court on October 23, when a trial date is expected.
